1 - Sanjay Gadpale S/o Late Ram Avatar Gadpale, Aged About 34 Years R/o
 Jamkot Para, Kondagaon, District Kondagaon, Chhattisgarh.

---- P  versus  1 - State Of Chhattisgarh Through Police Station Narayanpur, District  Narayanpur, Chhattisgarh.
 ---- Resp For Applicant : Mr. Manoj Paranjpe, Advocate For Respondent : Mr. Rajeev Bharat, Govt.
Advocate Hon'ble Shri Justice Parth Prateem Sahu Order On Board 12/11/2024 1.

Applicant has filed this first bail application under Section 483 of the Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for grant of regular bail as he has been arrested in connection with Crime No. 101 of 2023, registered at Police Station - Narayanpur, District - Narayanpur (C.G.) for offence punishable under Section 409, 420, 467, 468, 471 of the Indian Penal Code.

2. Case of the prosecution, in brief, is that the applicant, who is an employee of the Fisheries Department, posted in the office of the Assistant Director, Fisheries, District Narayanpur, as Assistant Grade- by BALRAM II, has misappropriated an amount of 81,84,200/- by forging documents and transferring the funds from the government account to his own account.
3.

Learned counsel for applicant submits that applicant is not pressing this bail application on merits and is only seeking bail on the ground of delay in trial and the period of pretrial detention of applicant for about one year and two months.

It is contended that charges has been framed by learned trial Court on 28.03.2024 and the case was fixed for evidence on 08.04.2024, however, only two witnesses have been examined till date out of 40 enlisted witnesses.
Applicant is in jail since 02.09.2023.
Hence, applicant may be released on bail.

sentences.text: 4. Learned State counsel opposes the submission of learned counsel for applicant and would submit that applicant is an employee of Fisheries Department and as per allegation, petitioner by forging documents has withdrawn amount from the government account and has transferred the same in his own account.
Documentary evidence in this regard has been collected by the investigating agency.
He contended that total misappropriation of funds is to the tune of Rs.81,84,200/-.
Therefore, applicant is not entitled to be released on bail.
5. I have heard learned counsel for the parties.
6. This bail application is filed on the ground of delay in trial and period of pretrial detention of applicant since 02.09.2023.

Perusal of the order sheet would show that on 28.03.2024, learned trial Court has framed the charges against applicant and fixed the case for recording of evidence of prosecution witnesses on 08.04.2024.
On the said date, i.e. first date fixed for recording of statement of witnesses, two witnesses namely Mohan Lal Rana and Laurence Tirkey were examined.
Perusal of the order sheet further shows that thereafter, the prosecution witnesses did not appear.

7. Considering the period of pretrial detention of applicant and also considering the fact that he being the government servant, there is no likelihood of his absconding, except two, no other witnesses have been examined till date, without commenting anything on merits of the case, I am inclined to enlarge the applicant on bail.

8. Accordingly, the bail application filed under Section 483 of Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita,
2023 is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant shall be released on regular bail upon furnishing a bail bond in the sum of Rs.25,000/- with one local surety in the like sum to the satisfaction of the Court below on the conditions that:-
a). Applicant shall appear before the trial Court regularly on each and every date,
unless exempted from appearance.
(b). Applicant shall not, in any manner, tamper with the prosecution witnesses.
c).
If the applicant is found involved in similar offence in the future, it will be open for the State to apply for cancellation of Bail.
Certified copy as per rules.
